# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 33 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 33 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_033_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 5, Chapter 1 — Patience and Anger

**1** "Be patient and long-suffering," he said, "and you will have dominion over all wickedness and will perform all righteousness. **2** For if you are patient, the Holy Spirit who dwells in you will be pure, not being darkened by any other evil spirit, but dwelling in a wide open space and rejoicing, and with the vessel in which he dwells he will serve the Lord in great cheerfulness, having peace within himself. **3** But if any angry temper comes in, at once the Holy Spirit, who is sensitive, feels cramped; not having a clean place, he seeks to depart. For he is choked by the evil spirit, not having room to serve the Lord as he wishes, being polluted by the angry temper. For the Lord dwells in patience, but the devil dwells in anger. **4** Both spirits then dwelling in the same place — when the one who is angry enters, the Holy Spirit is grieved and drives the Holy Spirit away from that person. **5** The spirit of patience is dear to God and acceptable to him, and in it the Lord dwells. The spirit of anger, however, is unprofitable, and it destroys the person in whom it dwells."

---

*EMET note: Mandate 5.1 — the pneumatological framework for patience vs. anger. The Holy Spirit is described as "sensitive" (hapalos = tender/delicate) — crowded out by the angry spirit. The Lord dwells in patience; the devil in anger. This is a remarkable pneumatology of the virtues and vices.*
